context.exploration_scope: Wired S12's Trigger-first check into the actual Decision-candidate search pipeline: re-confirmed state via the same E40+S11 baselines, and only if changed would re-search Decision Context and generate a verified candidate

problem: S12 established the Trigger check in isolation; it was unverified whether that check actually gates the downstream Decision-candidate search correctly, i.e. whether a real change would correctly flow into a verified candidate, and whether no-change correctly skips that search entirely rather than running it wastefully.

decision.decision_summary: Re-confirmed state via the same E40+S11 baselines (reused, not re-derived): 0 changes. NO_STATE_CHANGE maintained -- Decision Context search not exercised. 0 existing DEFERRED/RESOLVED verdicts force-changed, 0 automatic execution. Verdict: NO_STATE_CHANGE.

action.action_summary: Re-confirmed real-state change using S12's exact baseline method; gated the Decision Context re-search and candidate generation behind that Trigger; verified evidence_refs and provenance for any generated candidate before recording it.

result.note: No real change correctly skipped the downstream Decision Context search entirely, matching the Trigger-first discipline established at S12/E45.

cause.root_cause_summary: A Trigger check that exists but is not actually wired to gate the expensive downstream search is not yet load-bearing -- this phase closes that gap by making the search conditional on the Trigger result, not just informed by it.

lesson: A Trigger-first check only pays off once it actually gates the expensive work downstream. Verifying that gating explicitly -- not just running the check and the search unconditionally side by side -- is what makes the discipline real rather than decorative.
